findings.title: Typo in authenticator alias 'delayed-suthenticator-config'
findings.body: The alias for the 'delayed-authenticator' execution is set to 'delayed-suthenticator-config' (with the substring 'suthenticator' instead of 'authenticator'). The alias should be 'delayed-authenticator-config' to be consistent with the authenticator ID it labels. This is a naming typo and does not affect functionality, but should be corrected.

findings.title: Recovery codes are not consumed after use; the same code can be reused indefinitely
findings.body: In the isValid method for recovery codes (lines 326-340), the code returns true if any stored code equals the input via 'generatedKeys.stream().anyMatch(key -> key.equals(input.getChallengeResponse()))' but never removes or marks the consumed code. This breaks the single-use property of recovery codes - the same code can be used to log in as many times as desired. It also breaks the downstream logic in RecoveryAuthnCodesFormAuthenticator.isRecoveryAuthnCodeInputValid: because the RecoveryAuthnCodesCredentialModel reconstructed from the credential data has no 'used' codes, allCodesUsed() always returns false, so the CONFIGURE_RECOVERY_AUTHN_CODES required action is never triggered and the credential is never replaced. The local RecoveryAuthnCodesCredentialProvider handles this correctly; the test storage provider should mirror that behavior (e.g., by removing the consumed code from the stored list or tracking a used-codes list) so that tests against a federated user storage actually exercise the production behavior.

findings.title: testRecoveryKeysSetupAndLogin only exercises the happy path
findings.body: The new testRecoveryKeysSetupAndLogin only verifies that setup succeeds and that a single recovery code can be used to log in. It does not verify: (1) an invalid recovery code is rejected, (2) a recovery code cannot be reused once consumed (the single-use property), (3) when all recovery codes are consumed the user is prompted to set up new ones via the CONFIGURE_RECOVERY_AUTHN_CODES required action, (4) recovery codes can be disabled or removed via admin REST or the account console, or (5) the logoutOtherSessions=false branch of setupRecoveryKeysForUserWithRequiredAction. Given that this is the first end-to-end test for recovery codes in a federated storage, these negative and lifecycle cases should be covered.

findings.title: Recovery codes cannot be disabled through the standard mechanism
findings.body: disableCredentialType only handles OTP credentials; recovery codes fall through to the else branch and are simply logged as 'Unsupported to disable credential of type: ...'. Likewise, getDisableableCredentialTypesStream (lines 255-264) only adds CredentialModel.OTP. If a caller (e.g. admin REST or the account console) attempts to disable recovery codes for a user backed by this storage, the call silently does nothing while still returning success, leaving stale recovery codes in place. Recovery codes should be supported here the same way OTP is (set myUser.recoveryCodes = null and include RecoveryAuthnCodesCredentialModel.TYPE in the disableable types when present).
